title: Finite-presentation factorization through standard smooth reduction
statement:
theorem exists_standardSmooth_reduction_factorization_core
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (Λ : Type (max u v)) [CommRing Λ] [Algebra R Λ]
    (I : Ideal R)
    (hΛ : ObjectProperty.ind.{max u v}
      (fun C : CommAlgCat.{max u v} (R ⧸ I) ↦ IsStandardSmooth (R ⧸ I) C)
      (CommAlgCat.of (R ⧸ I) (Λ ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R Λ))))
    (A : Type w) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [FinitePresentation R A]
    (φ : A →ₐ[R] Λ) :
    ∃ (C : Type (max u v w)) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra R C),
      FinitePresentation R C ∧
      ∃ (ι : A →ₐ[R] C) (φ' : C →ₐ[R] Λ), φ'.comp ι = φ ∧
        IsStandardSmooth (R ⧸ I) (C ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R C))

proof.text: Base change finite presentation along R -> R/I and use Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor to identify the result with A/IA. Construct the reduced map by the quotient universal property and extend scalars along the surjection R -> R/I.

Replace the reduced source by a finite polynomial quotient over R/I, using Algebra.FinitePresentation.iff, and ULift this quotient and the base into the diagram universe. The explicit equivalence between CommAlgCat over R/I and commutative rings under the lifted base, followed by the under-category forgetful functor, preserves the filtered colimit. Apply RingHom.EssFiniteType.exists_eq_comp_ι_app_of_isColimit to the lifted source, and transfer the stage map back along the source equivalence. The chosen stage is standard smooth by the given diagram hypothesis; no increase in the target diagram universe is required.

Give the chosen standard smooth stage its A/IA-algebra structure through the factor map. It is finitely presented over R/I, while A/IA is finite type over R/I, so Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_restrict_scalars_finitePresentation yields finite presentation over A/IA. Apply the proved private general lifting lemma exists_lifted_presentation, which works for any finitely presented A/IA-algebra C and any ring map to Lambda/I Lambda compatible with phi on A. It chooses Presentation.exists_presentation_fin, lifts each relation coefficientwise by MvPolynomial.map_surjective, and lifts variable images by quotient surjectivity. Polynomial induction proves compatibility of evaluation and reduction; the relations therefore evaluate into I Lambda. The helper returns an A/IA-algebra equivalence of the reduced presentation quotient with C, without smoothness assumptions. Restrict that equivalence to R/I and transport the standard smoothness of this particular stage.

Apply the proved private exists_sum_of_mem_ringHom_map, valid for every ring homomorphism f and image ideal I.map f, to f = algebraMap R Lambda. Its proof uses Finsupp.mem_ideal_span_range_iff_exists_finsupp and enumeration of finite support to express each lifted relation evaluation as a finite sum of epsilon_ij * mu_ij with epsilon_ij in I. Construct the existing explicit PopescuCorrectionQuotient, with old variables sent to their lifted images and correction variables sent to mu_ij. Evaluation kills each corrected relation by these finite-sum identities. Descend evaluation to the quotient and define the inclusion of A via constant polynomials. Extensionality on A proves the composite is phi, and the finitely generated relation ideal gives finite presentation of the quotient over R.

Apply Algebra.nonempty_popescuCorrectionQuotient_reduction_equiv to identify the reduction of the explicit corrected quotient with a finite polynomial extension of the reduced stage presentation. The source-library MvPolynomial.isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension instance makes this extension standard smooth over that presentation. Algebra.IsStandardSmooth.trans makes it standard smooth over R/I, and Algebra.IsStandardSmooth.of_algEquiv transfers this to the corrected reduction. The ULift of the finite correction-variable set fixes the carrier universe at max u v w. These constructions allow empty lists, the zero ring and I=top, and require no nilpotence assumption.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07CK (lemma-lift-once), construction of A-prime through the displayed reduction isomorphism; finite-presentation stage argument adapted from Algebra.exists_smooth_factorization_of_ind_smooth, with a small polynomial quotient to accommodate arbitrary source universes; repair of duplicate-helper rejection: general coefficientwise presentation lifting for arbitrary reduced algebras and finite-sum membership for arbitrary ring homomorphisms
